title: HCP — Revocation Notice — payload
description: The request payload of the HCP 2.0-draft-3 revocation notification (HCP 6.2.3, 9.9): a provider tells a Context Client that a grant it held has been revoked. Carries the Security Event Token's `jti` as `noticeId` and the members of the `https://hcp.example/spec/events/grant-revoked` event; the Security Event Token claims map to the framework envelope (see the spec). The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

noticeId.description: The Security Event Token's `jti` (HCP 9.9): identifies the notice. The provider mints it fresh for each notice and keeps it the same on every delivery attempt of that notice, while each attempt is a new document with its own `id`, `issuedAt` and `proof`. The client deduplicates on it: an attempt whose `noticeId` it has already processed is acknowledged and not acted on again. Carrying `jti` in the payload rather than as the document `id` is pending HCP confirmation.

grantId.description: The grant-revoked event's `grantId`: the grant that was revoked or ended.

revokedAt.description: The grant-revoked event's `revokedAt`: when the provider revoked the grant. The revocation took effect then, whether or not this notice is delivered (HCP 6.2.3). For a grant that ended with its delegation (`reason` `delegation-ended`), the instant the delegation ended (HCP 17.6).

reason.description: How the grant ended. `revoked`: the grant was revoked (HCP 6.2); an absent `reason` means the same. `delegation-ended`: the grant ended, with status `expired`, because the delegation it was authorized under ended (HCP 17.6); the value is the reason HCP's `grant.expired` audit event records (HCP 8.2). Never the delegation's own reason for ending. HCP's grant-revoked event has no such member: this carriage adds it, pending HCP confirmation.

Response.title: HCP — Revocation Notice — response payload
Response.description: The client accepted the notice. Carries RFC 8935's `202 Accepted`, which has no body, so the payload is the empty object. A refusal is a trust-task-error, not this shape.
